text:
maya: Heads-up, ran a short perf sweep on the "fused epilogue + qkv-packing" prototype and hit weird tail spikes with paged-KV workloads. attaching notes and a quick repro.

liam: Yikes, can you paste the repro and the numbers?

maya: Repro command (local dev box, A100, 40GB):
```
./bench_fused_attn --model gpt-like --seq_len 2048 --batch 8 --paged_kv on --epilogue fused --qkv_pack on --iters 200
```

maya: Summary: median token-throughput ~14.6k tokens/s (expected ~15.2k), p95 latency +38%, p99 latency +120%. CPU-side profiler shows big memcpy spikes at epilogue boundary and GPU L2 miss counters ~2x.

ash: Does it repro without paged_kv?

maya: Tried that. With paged_kv off throughput stable: median ~15.3k, p99 within 10%. So interaction looks specific to paged-KV + qkv pack + epilogue fusion combo.

liam: Interesting — maybe packing changes alignment and increases scattered loads when we page KV. Any flamegraphs?

maya: Short perf snippet from nvprof + simple host traces (trimmed):
```
GPU memcpy H2D: 1.2ms spikes at iteration boundaries
kernel fused_attn_epilogue_pack: avg 0.9ms, spike 2.8ms
L2_read_misses: 1.1e6 -> 2.3e6 (paged_kv on)
Host memcpy (epilogue output merges): increased 3x at spike points
```

tasha: Could be that packing forces wider contiguous writes which cross the page boundaries used by paged-KV allocator -> extra page faults / migration / cache-line churn.

ash: Also check batching heuristic: batcher might coalesce different sequence-len requests creating larger soft-batches that exacerbate page-churn. What was the batcher config?

maya: Default heuristics: dynamic coalesce up to 12 tokens, prefer same model, allow batch growth up to 1.5x backlog. For the run I had one client generating long sequences and a mix of short ones -> effective internal batch variance high.

liam: OK — plausible cause chain: qkv pack changes memory layout -> epilogue fused writes back different stride -> paged-kv triggers cross-page writes -> combined with variable batching you get hot-page thrash.

maya: Quick low-risk mitigation I tested: disable epilogue fusion when paged_kv_enabled and seq_len >= 1024. Result: p99 drops back to baseline, median matches. Performance hit small (3%) but p99 stable.

ash: Can we teach the kernel chooser to prefer non-packed epilogue for paged_kv workloads? patch suggestion: add rule to kernel chooser config.

liam: +1. Also add a metric-emitter in runtime to capture "epilogue_crosspage_faults" or at least L2 misses per model-route so we can detect at runtime and auto-fallback.

maya: Proposed chooser config diff (pseudo):
```json
{
  "chooser_rules": [
    {
      "cond": "paged_kv_enabled && seq_len >= 1024 && batch_size >= 4",
      "prefer_kernel": "epilogue_no_pack",
      "reason": "avoid cross-page thrash with fused epilogue+qkvpack"
    }
  ]
}
```

tasha: Can we make it less brittle? maybe base on observed L2 miss rate > threshold instead of hard seq_len?

maya: Yeah I left that in the follow-up: if L2_miss_rate > 1e6 over last 100 iters, trigger fallback. But that requires exposing GPU counters into the runtime metrics pipeline (small infra work).

devbot: deploy-bench run queued: bench-fallback-rule-smoke #4521 (will run on dedicated-nightly infra).

liam: Also add a unit test that fuzzes alignment: random offsets with paged_kv on, check no page-scan spikes > 2x baseline.

maya: TODOs:
- maya: open PR for chooser rule + test (WIP)
- liam: add metric emitter plumbing for L2 misses (infra ticket)
- ash: add fuzz test harness for paged-kv alignment cases
- tasha: run longer soak on nightly with the fallback enabled to confirm no regressions for short-seq heavy workloads

ash: One more note: there was a variance across GPU driver versions in our quick check — on driver 535 the issue was worse than 540. We should pin driver in the nightly matrix.

maya: Thanks team. I'll push the PR draft and add the micro-bench logs. cc @tasha for soak runs. :thumbsup:

tasha: Roger. starting soak tonight around 01:00 PT. will report p95/p99 before tomorrow standup.

liam: If soak looks good we can make default chooser change behind feature-flag and roll out to dedicated next week.

maya: Added PR link: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/runtime/+/1234 (draft)

ash: Nice work catching this interaction. Glad we have a low-risk fallback path.

maya: End of thread — keeping logs attached in the PR.
